requested_by: CEO (founder ruling: Interlochen Review is a separate entity from Interlochen Arts Camp and is NOT covered by the previous hold)
what_it_actually_is_verbatim: 'The Interlochen Review is an online literary journal produced by the creative writing students of Interlochen Arts Academy.'
separate_entity_confirmation: CONFIRMED SEPARATE from Interlochen Arts Camp, and the distinction is substantive, not nominal: the Review is a free-to-read online literary journal that ACCEPTS SUBMISSIONS FROM HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS WORLDWIDE. Attending Interlochen is not required to submit — the Academy connection is on the EDITORIAL side (the journal is edited by Interlochen's creative writing students), not the contributor side. Interlochen Arts Camp is a paid summer programme; this is a publication venue anyone may submit to. They share a name and nothing else that matters for a student's decision.
what_it_publishes: Poetry, nonfiction, fiction, hybrid genres, script/screenplay, visual art, portfolios, songs, and interviews. Submission limits: fiction and nonfiction below 5,000 words; scripts/screenplays below 40 pages; visual art up to 10 individual pieces or one portfolio of up to 20.
eligibility_verbatim: 'Talented high school writers, singer-songwriters and artists (grades 9-12 or high school postgraduate year) from around the world.'
eligibility_note: Includes a 'high school postgraduate year', broader than the usual 9-12. Note the contrast with CJSJ, which explicitly bars graduates.
cost_note: No fee is stated on the landing page or the submission page. Did NOT find a 'free to submit' statement either. Given how much of this lane's work turned on undisclosed fees, recorded as unknown rather than assumed free — even though a school-run student literary journal charging a fee would be unusual.
anonymity_practice_verbatim: 'All submissions must be accompanied by a brief author or artist bio.' Name should appear only in the bio.
anonymity_note: Implies blind reading of the work itself — a small but real quality signal that this is edited seriously rather than as a vanity venue.
cycle_status_verbatim: 'Currently not open for submissions. Check back in January, 2027.'
deadline_note: No date published; the journal states only that submissions reopen in January 2027. That is an official 'check back', not a rolling intake.
selectivity: NOT STATED. No acceptance rate published.
category_verdict: DOES NOT BELONG IN `research`. It publishes no scientific or scholarly research of any kind — it is a literary and visual arts journal. It is ALSO a publication venue rather than an opportunity to DO something, so it hits the same taxonomy gap as the six student journals (no `publication_venue` value exists in the live `opportunity_category` enum).
value_verdict: GENUINELY VALUABLE — for the right student. Free-to-submit (probably), worldwide, real editorial selection, and it accepts songwriting and visual art portfolios, not just prose. For a student whose strength is creative writing or art, this is a credible external validation route, and ORYN currently has very little for such students. The problem was never that this row is worthless; it is that it was filed where it can only mislead.
recommendation: Remove from `research`; set cycle_status='closed'; keep the record and re-file it wherever arts/writing publication ends up living. If it stays in the corpus it should surface for a creative-writing interest, never for a research gap.
hold_scope_note: I evaluated ONLY The Interlochen Review. I did not research, touch, or draw any conclusion about Interlochen Arts Camp, which remains a separate entity under hold.
unresolved: Whether any submission fee exists — not stated either way on the pages retrieved.
